docs.title: HD Active
docs.text: Prevent external HD's from becoming inactive (sleeping).

docs.title: About
docs.text:
The functionality of this project, as stated above, is to prevent external mechanical Hard Drives from sleeping and avoid waiting for them to spin up when accessing.

The objectives of this project, however are the following:

  • Learn some QT basics for UI development in Python.
  • Use MkDocs and the theme MkDocs-Material for documentation.
  • Use PyInvoke for misc tasks in lieu of the more widely used Makefile. This has the following advantages: * Avoid the use of a different language for scripting. * Scripts are OS independent by using Python instead of an OS specific language like bash. * Scripts are easier to create and maintain (because Python ). * Other functionality that PyInvoke provides.
  • CI with GitHub Actions.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
hd_active                  # Run in the system tray (same as `hd_active gui`)
hd_active run              # Run in the console, without UI, until Ctrl+C
hd_active config init --drive e:\ --drive f:\ --wait 30
hd_active config show

Options common to all commands: --conf FILE (default: hd_active.ini in the current directory) and --log LEVEL. gui and run also accept --dry-run, to not write to the drives. See hd_active --help for more.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
Command Description hd_active gui Run in the system tray. This is the default if no command is given. Settings are changed in the Settings dialog and saved to the config file. hd_active run Run in the console, without UI, until interrupted with Ctrl+C. Doesn't need a display. hd_active config show Print the settings in the config file. hd_active config init Create a config file. Options: --drive PATH (multiple allowed), --wait SECONDS, --run-on-start, --force.

python -m hd_active is equivalent to hd_active.

Options:

  • --conf FILE: Config file to use. Default is hd_active.ini in the current directory.
  • --dry-run: Do everything except writing to the drives. Useful for trying things out. Can also be enabled by setting the HD_ACTION_DEBUG environment variable to true.
  • --log LEVEL: One of debug, info, warning (default), error.

docs.title: Config file
docs.text:
The file hd_active.ini, in the current directory by default (use --conf for a different one), is used to persist settings.

The file is created/updated when settings are changed in the UI. It can also be created with hd_active config init or by hand.

Options:

  • run_on_start: Whether HD Active should start pinging drives when the UI starts. If False, the user needs to click Start. Not used by hd_active run, which always starts.
  • wait_between_access: Time, in seconds, to wait between drive pings. If too long, the drives may go to sleep, if too short, drives will be pinged unnecessarily, although this is not a big issue.
  • drives: Which drives to ping. This is a comma separated list and doesn't need to have quotes, ex: e,f,g or e:\, f:\, g:\.

Sample: 

[HD Active]
run_on_start = True
wait_between_access = 30
drives = e:\, f:\, g:\

docs.title: Development
docs.text:
To get started with development of this project:

  1. Clone
  2. Install uv, which manages the Python version, virtual environment (.venv) and dependencies.
  3. uv sync
  4. uv run inv precommit install

Prefix commands with uv run (ex: uv run inv --help) or activate the .venv first.

docs.title: UI
docs.text:
This project uses Qt 6 for its UI components.

Qt Designer is used to create the UI, which outputs a .ui file (XML content that describes the UI). This file is then transformed into a .py file.

All the required tools are available by installing pyside6:

  • Qt Designer: pyside6-designer
  • .ui > .py Converter: pyside6-uic
  • .qrc > .py Converter (resources, like images): pyside6-rcc

These are wrapped in inv tasks: 

uv run inv ui edit settings_dialog   # Open in Qt Designer
uv run inv ui py                     # assets/ui/*.ui  > src/hd_active/ui/forms/ui_*.py
uv run inv ui rc                     # assets/*.qrc    > src/hd_active/ui/forms/*_rc.py
The generated files under src/hd_active/ui/forms should not be edited by hand.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
• HdActive (hd_active.py) is the engine. It doesn't depend on Qt and does the writing in a background thread.
  • HdActiveController (ui/controller.py) wraps the engine in a QObject and exposes what happens in it as Qt signals, delivered in the GUI thread.
  • The tray icon and the dialogs only talk to the controller: they call its slots and connect to its signals, never polling the engine nor touching widgets from the background thread.
  • Dialogs have a generated form (self.ui = Ui_...()) instead of inheriting from it.
  • Images are loaded from Qt resources (:/images/...), so they work regardless of how the app is installed.

To try the UI without writing to any drive: uv run hd_active --dry-run.

Note

Qt is not necessarily required, something like Tkinter could have been used (more open and included in Python), and the latest version of Qt (6) isn't necessary, something more established like Qt 5 could have been used, but I wanted to dip my toes into the Qt world and figured using the latest version would give me more lasting knowledge.

docs.title: Test
docs.text: pytest is used for testing and main features used are fixtures, parameters and markers. When working on test cases, make sure you're familiar with how these work.

docs.title: Markers
docs.text:
Markers are used to distinguish tests with pytest.mark.<marker_name>.

List of markers used, defined in pyproject.toml

Marker Description windows Test case valid on Windows operating system only.

docs.title: Linting and type checking
docs.text:
Ruff is used for linting and formatting and ty for type checking. Configuration for both is in pyproject.toml.

uv run inv lint all           # Fix and format (ruff), then type check (ty)
uv run inv lint all --check   # Check only, as done in CI

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text:
Dependencies are declared in pyproject.toml and locked in uv.lock.

uv add <package>                  # Add a runtime dependency
uv add --group dev <package>      # Add a dev dependency
uv lock --upgrade                 # Upgrade all dependencies
uv lock --upgrade-package <pkg>   # Upgrade one dependency
uv sync                           # Sync the environment with the lock file

docs.title: Development tasks
docs.text: This project uses typer-invoke (inv) to facilitate executing miscellaneous tasks that help with development.

docs.title: Using inv
docs.text:
List all available tasks: 

uv run inv --help

Help with a certain task: 

uv run inv lint --help

Use --dry to see what the task does without executing it.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
Install documentation requirements with: 

uv sync --group docs

You can then edit the .md files under the docs directory and, if more need to be added, update mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: View locally
docs.text:
• Web server (recommended) 
    mkdocs serve
  • Static files 
    mkdocs build
    This generates a static website under /site, which is in .gitignore.

docs.title: Update in GitHub
docs.text:
Simply run the command below to push the documentation to GitHub pages.

mkdocs gh-deploy

More instructions here.

The first time gh-deploy is used, authorization needs to be granted to publish to GitHub Pages. A GitHubCredentials widget appears and follow the prompts.

Documentation available here: https://joaonc.github.io/hd_active

When running this command, it's this website that needs to be updated (unless working in a forked project). Until a process is established for other people to update this GitHub Page location, please contact me and I'll push the documentation changes as needed.

docs.title: Release process
docs.text:
Using invoke tasks to help with the build/release workflow:

For a list of tasks: 

inv --list build

docs.title: Manually / Locally
docs.text: The individual steps are described here in case something needs to be done with adjustments in the steps.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
1. Bump version 
    inv build.version
    Then select which portion to bump (major, minor or patch).
  2. Create / merge a PR

docs.title: Package
docs.text:
1. Publish package to Pypi. 
    inv build.publish
    Gets published to https://pypi.org/project/hd_active/
